overview.text: Kinetic energy is the energy associated with motion: a moving ball, flowing water, or spinning wheel can possess it. For an object moving as a whole in translational motion, its kinetic energy is KE = ½mv², where m is mass and v is speed; the unit is the joule. Because speed is squared, doubling speed gives four times as much translational kinetic energy, while doubling mass at the same speed doubles it. A rotating rigid object also has rotational kinetic energy, KE = ½Iω², where I reflects how its mass is distributed around the axis and ω is angular speed. As an object falls, gravitational potential energy can change into kinetic energy.

key_facts.text: Translational kinetic energy is KE = ½mv²; m is mass and v is speed. Its SI unit is the joule.
At the same mass, doubling an object's speed makes its translational kinetic energy four times greater.
For a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis, rotational kinetic energy is KE = ½Iω²; I is moment of inertia and ω is angular speed.
Moment of inertia depends on how much mass lies at different distances from the rotation axis; mass farther from the axis contributes more.
A rolling object can have both translational and rotational kinetic energy; as it rolls downhill, gravitational potential energy can become both forms.
